title: Quentin Tarantino Confirms He's Written Script for His Tenth Film, Variety Reports
body:
Quentin Tarantino has confirmed that the script for his long‑awaited tenth feature film is already finished, but the celebrated director says production will remain on hold until his current stage venture, *The Killers of the Flower Moon* adaptation, closes its Broadway run. The revelation, made during a recent interview, offers a rare glimpse into the final chapter of a career that has reshaped modern cinema, while also underscoring the meticulous timing Tarantino has always applied to his projects.

The “Pulp Fiction” auteur, who has repeatedly stated that his tenth film will be his last, told reporters that the screenplay is “complete on paper” and that he is “satisfied with where it ends.” However, he added that the script will not see any further development until the play—his first foray into live theatre—finishes its scheduled engagements. The decision reflects Tarantino’s belief that his creative energy should not be split between two demanding mediums at once, and it aligns with his history of taking extended pauses between films to perfect each work.

Tarantino’s tenth film has been a subject of speculation for years, with fans and industry insiders piecing together clues from his interviews, social media posts, and the thematic arcs of his previous nine movies. While the exact genre and storyline remain under wraps, the director hinted that the new project will return to the gritty, dialogue‑driven storytelling that defined early works such as *Reservoir Dogs* and *Jackie Brown*. He also suggested that the film may explore a period setting, a motif he has revisited in recent projects like *Once Upon a Time in Hollywood* and the upcoming *Killers of the Flower Moon* stage adaptation.

The timing of the announcement is noteworthy. Tarantino’s play, a dramatization of the 1930s murder mystery that inspired the 2023 Scorsese film, opened on Broadway earlier this year and has been praised for its meticulous production design and faithful homage to the source material. By prioritising the stage production, Tarantino not only honors the theatrical roots of storytelling but also avoids the logistical challenges of juggling two major undertakings. Industry analysts see this as a strategic move that could preserve the quality and anticipation surrounding his final film, preventing the fatigue that can accompany overly rapid output.

Fans have expressed both excitement and impatience. Social media buzz surged after the interview, with hashtags like #Tarantino10 and #ScriptReady trending worldwide. Critics note that Tarantino’s decision to wait until the play’s curtain call could actually heighten anticipation, allowing the narrative to mature in the public imagination. Moreover, the director’s reputation for delivering meticulously crafted cinema—often with a modest number of takes and a distinct visual style—suggests that the final script will be a polished blueprint ready for immediate production once the theatrical commitment ends.

Looking ahead, the countdown to Tarantino’s swan song has officially begun. With the script in hand and the play set to close by mid‑2027, the window for filming could open as early as late 2027 or early 2028, depending on scheduling and financing. Studios are already positioning themselves to partner with the filmmaker, aware that the final Tarantino film will likely become a cultural milestone and a lucrative box‑office event. As the director continues to balance his theatrical ambitions with the promise of his ultimate cinematic statement, the industry watches closely, ready for the moment when the legend steps back from the director’s chair after a career that has forever altered the language of film.
